title: From a meeting to a working document
description: Checking the decisions against the recording and passing structured notes on in the format you need.

blocks.text: After the conversation a person checks the decisions that were proposed and clarifies the speakers and the wording. Every disputed item can be opened in the recording, and the confirmed text can be passed on to where the team actually works.

quote.text: it stopped being able to upload summaries with proper formatting to Day One and OneNote. Now, for OneNote, I have to email it to myself, cope and paste, and then re-bullet which is super cumbersome.

blocks.text: The first version is worth limiting to one useful transfer format: headings, lists and the edits made are all preserved. Reproducing that document on the recipient’s side matters more than adding a dozen nominal integration buttons.
Not losing the proofreading in transit

The app can prepare material for a discussion, but it must not declare a phrase it found automatically to be an agreed decision. If everything has to be labeled again after export, the work has simply moved from one editor to another.
